results.title: Orientable surface relator

results.summary: For $g \ge 0$, the orientable surface relator of genus $g$ is the element $[a_1, b_1] [a_2, b_2] \cdots [a_g, b_g]$ of the free group on the $2g$ generators $a_1, \dots, a_g, b_1, \dots, b_g$, where $[a, b] = a b a^{-1} b^{-1}$; for $g = 0$ it is the identity.

results.title: Groups satisfying a set of laws in countably many variables
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F_\mathbb{N}$ be the free group on countably many generators and $W \subseteq F_\mathbb{N}$ a set of words, the laws. A group $G$ satisfies the laws $W$ when $\varphi(w) = 1$ for every $w \in W$ and every homomorphism $\varphi \colon F_\mathbb{N} \to G$, that is, every law takes the value $1$ under every substitution of elements of $G$ for the variables. The variety defined by $W$ is the class of these groups.

results.title: Verbal subgroup of a free group of finite rank
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $W$ be a set of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators, and let $F_r$ be the free group on $r$ generators. The verbal subgroup $V_W(F_r)$ of $F_r$ for $W$ is the normal closure in $F_r$ of all elements $\varphi(w)$ with $w \in W$ and $\varphi \colon F_\mathbb{N} \to F_r$ a homomorphism.

results.title: Relatively free group as a quotient of a free group
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Let $W$ be a set of laws in the free group $F_\mathbb{N}$ on countably many generators, and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. The free $r$-generator group $G_r$ of the variety defined by $W$ is the quotient $F_r / V_W(F_r)$ of the free group $F_r$ on $r$ generators by its verbal subgroup $V_W(F_r)$ for $W$.

results.title: Test set of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subset $S$ of a group $G$ is a test set when every endomorphism of $G$ that fixes every element of $S$ is bijective, that is, an automorphism of $G$.

results.title: Test rank of a group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has test rank $r \in \mathbb{N}$ when $G$ has a test set of cardinality $r$ and every test set of $G$ has cardinality at least $r$ (an infinite set counting as having cardinality $\infty$), that is, when the minimum of the cardinalities of the test sets of $G$ is $r$.

results.title: Fundamental discriminant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An integer $D$ is a fundamental discriminant if either $D$ is squarefree and $D \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, or $D = 4m$ for some squarefree integer $m$ with $m \equiv 2 \pmod 4$ or $m \equiv 3 \pmod 4$.

results.title: Kronecker symbol at two
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $D$, the Kronecker symbol of $D$ at $2$ is $0$ if $D$ is even, $1$ if $D \equiv \pm 1 \pmod 8$, and $-1$ if $D \equiv \pm 3 \pmod 8$.

results.title: Kronecker symbol at a prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $D$ and a natural number $p$, the Kronecker symbol of $D$ at $p$ is the Kronecker symbol of $D$ at two if $p = 2$, the Legendre symbol $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)$ if $p$ is an odd prime, and $0$ if $p$ is not prime.

results.title: Kronecker symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an integer $D$ and a natural number $n$, the Kronecker symbol $\left(\frac{D}{n}\right)$ is defined as follows. If $n = 0$, it is $1$ when $D = \pm 1$ and $0$ otherwise. If $n \ge 1$ and $n = p_1 p_2 \cdots p_k$ is the factorization of $n$ into primes, listed with multiplicity, it is the product of the Kronecker symbols of $D$ at the primes $p_1, \ldots, p_k$ (the empty product $1$ when $n = 1$).

results.title: Kronecker symbol with a prime denominator
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $D$ and every prime $p$, the Kronecker symbol $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)$ equals the Kronecker symbol of $D$ at the prime $p$.

results.title: Kronecker and Jacobi symbols agree at odd primes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every integer $D$ and every prime $p \ne 2$, the Kronecker symbol $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)$ equals the Jacobi symbol $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)$.

results.title: Quadratic Dirichlet character of a fundamental discriminant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be a fundamental discriminant. Then there is a unique integer-valued Dirichlet character $\chi$ modulo $|D|$ such that $\chi(n \bmod |D|) = \left(\frac{D}{n}\right)$ for every natural number $n$, where $\left(\frac{D}{n}\right)$ is the Kronecker symbol.

results.title: Quadratic reciprocity for the Kronecker symbol, positive $D \equiv 1 \pmod 4$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $D$ be a positive integer with $D \equiv 1 \pmod 4$ and let $p$ be an odd prime. Then the Jacobi symbol $\left(\frac{p}{|D|}\right)$ equals the Kronecker symbol $\left(\frac{D}{p}\right)$.

results.title: Genus of a compact Riemann surface
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a compact Riemann surface $X$, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$, the genus of $X$ is a natural number.

results.title: A compact Riemann surface has genus zero iff it is a sphere
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$. The genus of $X$ is $0$ if and only if $X$ is homeomorphic to the unit sphere in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$.

results.title: Jacobian of a compact Riemann surface
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a compact Riemann surface $X$, that is, a compact connected Hausdorff space with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$, the Jacobian $J(X)$ of $X$ is a type in the same universe as $X$.

results.title: Abel–Jacobi map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$. Each point $P \in X$ gives a map $X \to J(X)$, the Abel–Jacobi map based at $P$.

results.title: The Abel–Jacobi map is holomorphic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$, and let $J(X)$ be its Jacobian, a complex manifold modelled on $\mathbb{C}^g$. For every point $P \in X$, the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ is holomorphic.

results.title: The Abel–Jacobi map sends the base point to zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$, an abelian group. For every point $P \in X$, the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ sends $P$ to $0$.

results.title: The Abel–Jacobi map is injective in positive genus
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface with Jacobian $J(X)$, and let $P \in X$. If the genus of $X$ is positive, then the Abel–Jacobi map $X \to J(X)$ based at $P$ is injective.

results.title: Pushforward on Jacobians
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the Jacobian of $X$, an abelian group with a topology. For a holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the pushforward $f_*$ is a continuous group homomorphism from $J(X)$ to $J(Y)$. It is meant to be the homomorphism induced by $f$; its properties are stated separately.

results.title: The pushforward on Jacobians is holomorphic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, of genera $g_X$ and $g_Y$. The Jacobian $J(X)$ of $X$ is a complex-analytic manifold modeled on $\mathbb{C}^{g_X}$, and likewise $J(Y)$ on $\mathbb{C}^{g_Y}$. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the pushforward $f_* : J(X) \to J(Y)$ is holomorphic.

results.title: Pushforward along the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifold of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for its Jacobian. For every $P \in J(X)$, the pushforward of $P$ along the identity map of $X$ is $P$: $(\mathrm{id}_X)_*(P) = P$.

results.title: Pushforward respects composition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for the Jacobian of $X$. For all holomorphic maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ and every $P \in J(X)$, the pushforwards satisfy $(g \circ f)_*(P) = g_*(f_*(P))$.

results.title: The pullback map on Jacobians is holomorphic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces of genus $g_X$ and $g_Y$, with Jacobians $J(X)$ and $J(Y)$, complex manifolds modelled on $\mathbb{C}^{g_X}$ and $\mathbb{C}^{g_Y}$. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$, the induced pullback map $f^* : J(Y) \to J(X)$ is holomorphic.

results.title: Pullback along the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a compact Riemann surface, that is, a compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifold of dimension one, and write $J(X)$ for its Jacobian. For every $P \in J(X)$, the pullback of $P$ along the identity map of $X$ is $P$: $(\mathrm{id}_X)^*(P) = P$.

results.title: Pullback on Jacobians is compatible with composition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ be compact Riemann surfaces, and for a holomorphic map $h$ between compact Riemann surfaces write $h^*$ for the induced pullback map on Jacobians. For all holomorphic maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ and every point $P$ of the Jacobian $J(Z)$, we have $(g \circ f)^*(P) = f^*(g^*(P))$.

results.title: Degree of a holomorphic map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact connected Hausdorff spaces with a complex-analytic atlas modelled on $\mathbb{C}$. Every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$ has a degree, which is a natural number.

results.title: Pushforward of a pullback is multiplication by the degree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ and $Y$ be compact Riemann surfaces, that is, compact, connected, Hausdorff complex-analytic manifolds of dimension one, and write $J(Y)$ for the Jacobian of $Y$, an abelian group. For every holomorphic map $f : X \to Y$ and every $P \in J(Y)$, the pushforward along $f$ of the pullback of $P$ along $f$ is $\deg(f) \cdot P$, where the degree $\deg(f)$ is a natural number: $f_*(f^*(P)) = \deg(f) \cdot P$.

results.title: Convex sets of diameter one
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $K$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a unit-diameter convex set when it is nonempty and convex and its diameter $\sup_{x, y \in K} \lVert x - y \rVert$ is exactly $1$.

results.title: Covering a congruent copy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A planar set $\Omega$ covers a congruent copy of a planar set $K$ when some isometry $e$ of the plane onto itself satisfies $e(K) \subseteq \Omega$.

results.title: Universal convex covers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $\Omega$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is a universal convex cover when it is nonempty and convex and, for every nonempty convex set $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$ of diameter $1$, some isometry $e$ of the plane onto itself satisfies $e(K) \subseteq \Omega$.

results.title: Planar area
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The area of a set $S$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is its Lebesgue measure (outer measure if $S$ is not measurable), a value in $[0, \infty]$, so infinite area is allowed.

results.title: Areas of universal convex covers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The set of admissible cover areas is the set of all $a \in [0, \infty]$ for which there is a universal convex cover $\Omega$ in the plane (a nonempty convex set containing a congruent copy of every nonempty convex planar set of diameter $1$) whose Lebesgue area is $a$.

results.title: Directional width
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a planar set $K$ and a vector $u$ in the plane, the width of $K$ in direction $u$ is $\sup_{x \in K} \langle u, x \rangle - \inf_{x \in K} \langle u, x \rangle$, where the supremum and infimum are taken in $\mathbb{R}$, with the convention that each is $0$ when the set of values $\langle u, x \rangle$ is empty or unbounded on that side.

results.title: Sets of constant width one
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Euclidean 3-space
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with its Euclidean inner product and norm.

results.title: Ordered triple of points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the family indexed by $\{0, 1, 2\}$ that sends $0 \mapsto p$, $1 \mapsto q$ and $2 \mapsto r$.

results.title: Triangle on three affinely independent points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space whose ordered triple $(p, q, r)$ is affinely independent, the triangle in Euclidean 3-space with vertices $p$, $q$, $r$, in that order.

results.title: Extended circumradius of three points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is the following value in $[0, \infty]$. If $p, q, r$ are affinely independent, it is the circumradius of the triangle with vertices $p$, $q$ and $r$. Otherwise, that is, when the three points are collinear (in particular when two of them coincide), it is $\infty$.

results.title: Extended circumradius of a triangle
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p, q, r$ be points of Euclidean 3-space and let $T$ be a triangle in Euclidean 3-space whose vertices, in order, are $p$, $q$ and $r$. Then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ equals the circumradius of $T$.

results.title: Collinear points have infinite extended circumradius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $p, q, r$ are points of Euclidean 3-space and the set $\{p, q, r\}$ is collinear, then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is $\infty$.

results.title: Equal first two points give infinite extended circumradius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $p, q, r$ are points of Euclidean 3-space with $p = q$, then the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$ is $\infty$.

results.title: Extended circumradius is symmetric in the first two points
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(q, p, r)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.

results.title: Extended circumradius is symmetric in the last two points
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(p, r, q)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.

results.title: Extended circumradius is invariant under reversal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(r, q, p)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.

results.title: Translation invariance of the extended circumradius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every vector $v$ and all points $p, q, r$ of Euclidean 3-space, the extended circumradius of $(v + p, v + q, v + r)$ equals the extended circumradius of $(p, q, r)$.

results.title: Thickness
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The thickness of a set $s$ in Euclidean 3-space is the infimum, in $[0, \infty]$, of the extended circumradii of $(p, q, r)$ over all points $p, q, r \in s$. Since the extended circumradius of three collinear points (in particular of three points two of which coincide) is $\infty$, this is also the infimum over the triples of pairwise distinct points of $s$.

results.title: Thickness is at most every circumradius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $s$ in Euclidean 3-space and all points $p, q, r \in s$, the thickness of $s$ is at most the extended circumradius of $p, q, r$.

results.title: Thickness is antitone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $s \subseteq t$ are sets in Euclidean 3-space, then the thickness of $t$ is at most the thickness of $s$: enlarging a set can only add triples and hence can only decrease the infimum.

results.title: Thickness of the empty set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The empty subset of Euclidean 3-space has thickness $\infty$, as an empty infimum in $[0, \infty]$.

results.title: Thickness of a single point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every point $p$ of Euclidean 3-space, the set $\{p\}$ has thickness $\infty$: its only triple $(p, p, p)$ is degenerate.

results.title: Contour length
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\gamma$ be a map from $\mathbb{R}$ to Euclidean 3-space and let $a, b$ be real numbers. The contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ is the total variation of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$: the supremum, over all finite sequences $t_0 \le t_1 \le \dots \le t_n$ of points of $[a, b]$, of $\sum_{i < n} \lVert \gamma(t_{i+1}) - \gamma(t_i) \rVert$. It is a value in $[0, \infty]$.

results.title: Contour length of a $C^1$ curve
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a \le b$ be real numbers and let $\gamma$ be a map from $\mathbb{R}$ to Euclidean 3-space that is continuously differentiable on $[a, b]$. Then the contour length of $\gamma$ on $[a, b]$ equals $\int_a^b \lVert \gamma'(t) \rVert \, dt$.

results.title: Ropelength ratio

The quotient is taken in $[0, \infty]$, where $c / 0 = \infty$ for $c \ne 0$, $0 / 0 = 0$ and $c / \infty = 0$.

results.title: Tight alternating knot constant

results.title: Tight knot constant
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The tight knot constant $C_{22a}$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the set of real numbers $c$ that are admissible for the tight-knot inequality $\mathrm{ropelength} \ge c \cdot (\text{crossing number})^{3/4}$ on link types. results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The real number $0$ is admissible for the tight-knot inequality between the ropelength and the crossing number of link types.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Height-bounded derivations
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. For a sentential form $\alpha$ (a list of terminals and nonterminals of $g$), a terminal word $w$ and a natural number $n$, say that $\alpha$ yields $w$ at height $n$ when this follows from three rules: the empty form yields the empty word at every height $n$; if $\alpha$ yields $w$ at height $n$, then for every terminal $a$ the form $a\alpha$ yields $aw$ at height $n$; and if…

results.title: Raising the height bound of a yield
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, and $n \le m$, then $\alpha$ yields $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $m$.

results.title: Every yield has a height bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$, then there is a natural number $n$ such that $\alpha$ yields $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$.

results.title: Height-bounded yields are yields
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, then $\alpha$ yields $w$.

results.title: Concatenating height-bounded yields
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $u$ yields the terminal word $w_1$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, and a sentential form $v$ yields the terminal word $w_2$ through one of height at most $m$, then the concatenation $uv$ yields $w_1 w_2$ through a derivation forest of height at most $\max(n, m)$.

results.title: Splitting a height-bounded yield at a concatenation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $u$, $v$ sentential forms of $g$. If the concatenation $uv$ yields the terminal word $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, then there are terminal words $w_1$, $w_2$ with $w = w_1 w_2$ such that $u$ yields $w_1$ and $v$ yields $w_2$, each through a derivation forest of height at most $n$.

results.title: Length bound for height-bounded yields
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $R$ a natural number such that every production of $g$ has an output of length at most $R$. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, then $|w| \le |\alpha| \cdot \max(2, R)^n$.

results.title: Minimal-height derivation forests exist
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ yields the terminal word $w$, then there is a natural number $n$ such that $\alpha$ yields $w$ through a derivation forest of height at most $n$, but through no derivation forest of height at most $m$ for any $m < n$.

results.title: Derivation contexts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar, let $A$ and $B$ be nonterminals of $g$, and let $l$ and $r$ be words over the terminal alphabet. Then $(l, r)$ is a derivation context from $A$ to $B$ when, for every terminal word $w$ that the nonterminal $B$ yields in $g$, the nonterminal $A$ yields the word $l w r$ in $g$.

results.title: A production gives derivation contexts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and $A \to \alpha_1 B \alpha_2$ a production of $g$, where $B$ is a nonterminal and $\alpha_1$, $\alpha_2$ are sentential forms. If $\alpha_1$ yields the terminal word $l$ and $\alpha_2$ yields the terminal word $r$, then for every terminal word $w$ yielded by $B$ the word $l w r$ is yielded by $A$; that is, $(l, r)$ is a derivation context from $A$ to $B$.

results.title: Pumping through a self-context
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar, $A$ a nonterminal and $l$, $r$, $x$ terminal words. Suppose that for every terminal word $w$ yielded by $A$ the word $l w r$ is also yielded by $A$, and that $A$ yields $x$. Then for every natural number $i$ the nonterminal $A$ yields $l^i x r^i$, where $l^i$ and $r^i$ denote the concatenations of $i$ copies of $l$ and of $r$.

results.title: Pumping lemma for context-free languages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context-free language $L$ over an alphabet $T$ there is a natural number $n > 0$ such that every word $w \in L$ with $|w| \ge n$ can be written as $w = uvxyz$ with words $u, v, x, y, z$ over $T$ such that $vy$ is nonempty, $|vxy| \le n$, and $u v^i x y^i z \in L$ for every natural number $i$, where $v^i$ and $y^i$ denote the concatenations of $i$ copies of $v$ and of $y$.

results.title: Code of a URM instruction
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Code of a URM instruction as a natural number: the instruction tag paired with the paired arguments, `Z n ↦ pair 0 n`, `S n ↦ pair 1 n`, `T m n ↦ pair 2 (pair m n)`, `J m n q ↦ pair 3 (pair m (pair n q))`.

results.title: Tag of an instruction code
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every URM instruction $I$, unpairing the code of $I$ gives first component $0$ if $I$ is a zero instruction $Z\,n$, $1$ if it is a successor instruction $S\,n$, $2$ if it is a transfer $T\,m\,n$, and $3$ if it is a jump $J\,m\,n\,q$.

results.title: Payload of an instruction code
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $\langle a, b \rangle$ for the pairing of natural numbers $a$ and $b$. For every URM instruction $I$, unpairing the code of $I$ gives second component $n$ if $I$ is $Z\,n$ or $S\,n$, $\langle m, n \rangle$ if $I$ is $T\,m\,n$, and $\langle m, \langle n, q \rangle \rangle$ if $I$ is $J\,m\,n\,q$.

results.title: One coded URM step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A coded state is a program counter $k$ together with a list $r$ of register contents (in use, the contents of registers $0, \dots, R$, where $R$ is the register bound of the program), and a program is given by the list $c$ of its instruction codes. Write $c_k$ for entry $k$ of $c$, and $r_j$ for entry $j$ of $r$, read as $0$ when $j$ is past the end of $r$; setting an entry past the end of $r$ leaves $r$ unchanged.…

results.title: The coded step is primitive recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The coded step is primitive recursive, for any fixed list of instruction codes.

results.title: Register bound
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The register bound $R$ of a URM program $p$ is the sum, over the instructions of $p$, of the largest register index each instruction refers to. Every register that an instruction of $p$ can read or write is at most $R$.

results.title: Register list
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$, the register list of a register state $\sigma$ is the list $(\sigma(0), \sigma(1), \dots, \sigma(R))$ of the contents of registers $0, \dots, R$.

results.title: Coded machine state
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$, the coded state of a machine state $s$ is the pair consisting of the program counter of $s$ and the register list $(r_0, \dots, r_R)$ of the contents of registers $0, \dots, R$ of $s$.

results.title: Decoding a coded state
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A coded state is a pair $(c, \ell)$ of a natural number $c$ and a list $\ell$ of natural numbers. Its machine state has program counter $c$, and register $n$ holds the $n$-th entry of $\ell$ (counting from $0$) when $n$ is less than the length of $\ell$, and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Length of the register list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$ and a register state $\sigma$, the register list of $\sigma$ (the contents of registers $0, \dots, R$) has length $R + 1$.

results.title: Reading the register list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program with register bound $R$ and $\sigma$ a register state. For every $n$, the entry at position $n$ of the register list of $\sigma$, read with default $0$, is $\sigma(n)$ if $n \le R$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Updating a register updates the register list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program with register bound $R$, let $\sigma$ be a register state, and let $n \le R$ and $v$ be natural numbers. The register list of the state obtained from $\sigma$ by setting register $n$ to $v$ equals the register list of $\sigma$ with its entry at position $n$ replaced by $v$.

results.title: Instructions stay within the register bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$ and every instruction $I$ of $p$, the largest register index referenced by $I$ is at most $R$.

results.title: Written registers lie within the register bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program with register bound $R$. If an instruction of $p$ writes to register $n$, then $n \le R$.

results.title: Registers read by a program lie within the register bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program. If $n$ is a register read by some instruction of $p$, then $n$ is at most the register bound of $p$.

results.title: Decoding and re-encoding a coded state gives it back
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program with register bound $R$, and let $c$ be a coded state: a program counter together with a list of register contents. If the list has length $R + 1$, then the coded state, with respect to $p$, of the machine state decoded from $c$ is $c$.

results.title: A state that can step is running
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a state $s$ of a URM program $p$ makes a step to some state, then the program counter of $s$ is less than the number of instructions of $p$.

results.title: Instruction codes by position
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the URM program $p$ has instruction $I$ at position $pc$, then the entry at position $pc$ of the list of instruction codes of $p$, read with default $0$, is the code of $I$.

results.title: A machine step is a coded step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program, let $R$ be the sum over the instructions of $p$ of the largest register index each one mentions, and let $s'$ be a state that $p$ reaches from the state $s$ in one step. Then the coded step, run on the list of codes of the instructions of $p$, sends the coded state of $s$ (its program counter together with the list of the contents of its registers $0, \dots, R$) to the coded state of $s'$.

results.title: A coded step is a machine step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program and $s$ a machine state. If one coded URM step, run on the list of codes of the instructions of $p$ from the coded state of $s$, yields $c'$, then there is a machine state $s'$ such that $p$ steps from $s$ to $s'$ in one step and the coded state of $s'$ is $c'$.

results.title: URM-decidable predicate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is URM-decidable when some URM program computes its characteristic function: started on any input $n$ (register $0$ holding $n$, all other registers $0$), the program halts, and register $0$ then holds $1$ if $P(n)$ holds and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: URM-recognizable predicates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is URM-recognizable when there is a URM program that, started with input $n$ in register $0$ and every other register $0$, halts if and only if $P(n)$ holds.

results.title: One-step function on coded states
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list of instruction codes, the one-step function sends a coded state $s$ to the result of one coded URM step from $s$ when that step is defined, and leaves $s$ unchanged when it is not (in particular when $s$ is halted).

results.title: The one-step function is primitive recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list of natural numbers, read as instruction codes, the function on coded states (pairs of a program counter and a register list) that sends a coded state to its successor under one coded step, and a coded state with no successor to itself, is primitive recursive.

results.title: Bounded execution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a list of instruction codes, a number $t$ and a coded state $s$, bounded execution applies the one-step function for these codes $t$ times, starting from $s$.

results.title: Bounded execution unfolds by one step
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a list of instruction codes, a number $t$ and a coded state $s$, bounded execution for $t + 1$ steps from $s$ is the one-step function applied to the result of bounded execution for $t$ steps from $s$.

results.title: Initial coded state
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a URM program $p$ with register bound $R$ and an input $x$, the initial coded state has program counter $0$ and register list $(x, 0, \dots, 0)$ of length $R + 1$: register $0$ holds $x$ and registers $1, \dots, R$ hold $0$.

results.title: The initial coded state is primitive recursive in the input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The initial coded state is primitive recursive in the input.

results.title: Bounded execution is primitive recursive in the input and the step bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a URM program $p$, the bounded execution of $p$ for $t$ steps ($t$ iterations of the one-step function on the list of instruction codes of $p$), started from the initial coded state for input $x$, is a primitive recursive function of the pair $(x, t)$.

results.title: The initial coded state codes the initial machine state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a URM program $p$ and an input $x$, the initial coded state for $x$ equals the coded state of the initial machine state with input list $[x]$.

results.title: Bounded execution only reaches codes of reachable states
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program, $x$ an input and $t$ a natural number. Then there is a machine state $s'$, reachable from the initial state with input list $[x]$ by steps of $p$, whose coded state equals the result of bounded execution for $t$ steps on the instruction codes of $p$ from the initial coded state for $x$.

results.title: A halted coded state gives a halting machine run
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program, $x$ an input and $t$ a number. If bounded execution for $t$ steps on the instruction codes of $p$ from the initial coded state for $x$ reaches a program counter at least the length of the list of instruction codes, then $p$ halts on the input list $[x]$.

results.title: Every reachable state is reached by bounded execution
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a URM program and $x$ an input. If a machine state $s$ is reachable from the initial state with input list $[x]$ by steps of $p$, then for some number $t$, bounded execution for $t$ steps on the instruction codes of $p$ from the initial coded state for $x$ gives the coded state of $s$.

results.title: Bounded URM execution is stable once halted
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a list of instruction codes, $s$ a coded state and $t$ a natural number. If after $t$ steps of bounded execution of $c$ from $s$ the program counter is at least the length of $c$, then $t + 1$ steps of bounded execution of $c$ from $s$ give the same coded state as $t$ steps.

results.title: Bounded URM execution stays at its halted value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $c$ be a list of instruction codes, $s$ a coded state, and $t_1 \le t_2$ natural numbers. If after $t_1$ steps of bounded execution of $c$ from $s$ the program counter is at least the length of $c$, then $t_2$ steps of bounded execution of $c$ from $s$ give the same coded state as $t_1$ steps.

results.title: Output after a given number of steps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a URM program $p$, an input $x$ and a number $t$, run bounded execution for $t$ steps on the instruction codes of $p$ from the initial coded state for $x$. If the resulting program counter is less than the length of the list of instruction codes, the program is still running and there is no output; otherwise the output is the entry at position $0$ of the resulting register list, read with default $0$.

results.title: The URM output after a given number of steps is computable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every URM program $p$, the function sending an input $x$ and a step count $t$ to the output of $p$ on $x$ after $t$ steps (nothing while $p$ is still running, the contents of register $0$ once it has halted) is a computable function of the pair $(x, t)$.

results.title: A URM-computable partial function is partial recursive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a partial function from $\mathbb{N}$ to $\mathbb{N}$. Suppose some URM program has the following property for every natural number $x$: started with $x$ in register $0$ and all other registers $0$, it halts exactly when $f(x)$ is defined, and then it holds $f(x)$ in register $0$. Then $f$ is partial recursive.

results.title: A URM-decidable predicate is computable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a predicate $P$ on the natural numbers is URM-decidable, then it is a computable predicate: its Boolean decision function, sending $n$ to whether $P(n)$ holds, is computable.

results.title: A URM-recognizable predicate is recursively enumerable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A URM-recognizable predicate is recursively enumerable.

results.title: A URM-decidable predicate is decidable by a single-tape Turing machine
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A URM-decidable predicate is decidable by a single-tape Turing machine.

results.title: A URM-decidable predicate is decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A URM-decidable predicate is decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine.

results.title: A URM-recognizable predicate is recognizable by a single-tape Turing machine
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A URM-recognizable predicate is recognizable by a single-tape Turing machine.

results.title: A URM-recognizable predicate is recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A URM-recognizable predicate is recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.

results.title: A URM-computable total function is computed by a multi-stack Turing machine
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$. Suppose there is a URM program that, for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, started with $n$ in register $0$ and all other registers $0$, halts with $f(n)$ in register $0$. Then there is a multi-stack Turing machine that computes $f$ with input and output numbers written in binary: started on the binary word of $n$, it halts with the binary word of $f(n)$.

results.title: URM-decidability implies multi-stack decidability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$ that is URM-decidable is decidable by a multi-stack Turing machine.

results.title: URM-recognizability implies multi-stack recognizability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every predicate $P$ on $\mathbb{N}$ that is URM-recognizable is recognizable by a multi-stack Turing machine.
